task: Write a win-back email for users who haven't logged into our budgeting app in 90 days. We added bank sync for credit unions and a new weekly summary feature, and we want to offer 2 months free on the Pro plan with the code COMEBACK2. Keep the subject line under 45 characters and make the email feel like a human wrote it.

ambition:     A lifecycle copywriter would lead with the one reason a lapsed user might care now, not a feature list. For a budgeting app, people usually quit because their bank wouldn't connect, so credit union sync goes first and the weekly summary second. They would also write it as a plain, first-person note from a named sender, with one link and one code.
agency:       The raw material is the exit-survey answers, cancellation reasons, and support tickets that mention credit unions or failed bank connections, plus the release notes for what sync and the summary actually do. None of that is in reach here, so assume some lapsed users left over missing credit union support, write to that without citing numbers, and don't invent product details beyond the two features named.
acceleration: Use the standard win-back structure: acknowledge the gap without guilt, give one concrete new reason, make a low-friction offer, and add an easy out. Use a first-name merge tag, a preheader line that continues the subject, and plain-text styling instead of a designed template.
accuracy:     Outside checks: redeem COMEBACK2 on a lapsed test account to confirm it gives 2 months of Pro, send seed copies to Gmail and Apple Mail to check the subject isn't truncated on mobile, and have a teammate who hasn't seen it say whether it sounds like a person. Nothing inside the model can confirm the code works or how the email reads to a real user.

**Subject:** Still keeping an eye on your budget? (41 characters)

---

Hi [First name],

It's been a while since you last opened [App Name], so I wanted to check in. No guilt trip, I promise. Life gets busy, and budgeting is usually the first thing to slide.

If you're thinking about giving it another go, a couple of things have changed since you left:

**Bank sync now works with credit unions.** This was our most-requested feature, and it's finally here. If a credit union was the reason you stopped, it's worth another look.

**There's a new weekly summary.** Once a week you'll get a short snapshot of where your money went, with no digging through transactions. It takes about a minute to read.

To make coming back easier, here are **2 months of Pro on us**. Enter the code **COMEBACK2** at checkout and you're set.

[Button: Pick up where you left off]

Your old budgets and categories are still there, so you won't be starting from scratch.

If something about the app wasn't working for you, just reply to this email. It comes to me, and I read every response. Your feedback really does shape what we build next.

Either way, I hope things are going well.

Warmly,
[Your name]
[App Name]

---

**Notes:**
- The subject is 41 characters including spaces and punctuation.
- I wrote "your old budgets are still there" as a placeholder. Please confirm it's true for users inactive 90+ days, or cut that line.
- Add an expiration date for the code if there is one, for example "Use COMEBACK2 by [date]". That adds some urgency without sounding pushy.
- Send it from a real person's name and address rather than noreply, so the "just reply" line works.
answers.nudge:
# Win-back email: 90-day lapsed users

## Subject line

**Primary (33 characters):** `Missed you. Here's 2 months on us`

**A/B alternatives:**
| Angle | Subject | Chars |
|---|---|---|
| Feature-led | `Your credit union is now supported` | 35 |
| Curiosity | `What's new since you left (it's good)` | 37 |
| Low-key human | `Quick note from [First name] at [App]` | ~35 |

**Preheader (~60 chars):** `Credit union sync, weekly summaries, and Pro on us.`

---

## Email body

**From:** [Real person's name], [App Name] (not "The [App] Team")
**Reply-to:** a monitored inbox

Hi {{first_name}},

It's been a few months since you last opened [App], and I wanted to write you a short note.

Budgeting apps are easy to drop. Life gets busy, one month's spending gets messy, and the app starts to feel like homework. If that was you, no hard feelings.

A lot has changed since you left, though. Two of the changes are things people kept asking us for:

**Credit union bank sync.** You can now connect accounts from thousands of credit unions, so you don't have to enter transactions by hand. If that's what pushed you away, it's fixed.

**Weekly summary.** Every [Monday] you get a short recap of where your money went, with no need to log in and dig through charts. It takes about a minute to read, and it's the easiest way to keep up with a budget.

To make coming back easy, here are **2 months of Pro, free**. Use the code **COMEBACK2** at checkout. It doesn't need a credit card up front [confirm], and you can cancel anytime.

**[Button: Pick up where you left off →]**

If you'd rather tell me why you left, just reply to this email. I read every response, and it helps us make the app better.

Thanks,
[Name]
[Title], [App Name]

P.S. Your past budgets and categories are still there [confirm before sending], so you won't be starting from scratch.

*[Unsubscribe] · [Address]*

---

## Why it's written this way

- **Human voice:** It's a first-person note from a named sender, with no hero image, no "WE MISS YOU!" and no exclamation points. It's plain text with a single button, which usually does better for lapsed users than a designed template.
- **Cause, then cure:** It names the likely reason for leaving (manual entry, homework fatigue) and shows the two features as answers to it, instead of listing them.
- **No guilt:** The line "no hard feelings" lowers resistance.
- **One CTA:** The code appears once in the body and once in the button's destination. Pre-apply it in the link (`?promo=COMEBACK2`) so nobody has to type it.
- **Reply invitation:** It gives people who won't convert a way to give you churn feedback.

## Before you send

1. **Fill the brackets.** The "confirm" items are claims I can't verify: no card required, data retained, the weekly send day. Remove any that aren't true.
2. **Add an expiry.** A deadline is the strongest lever for a discount, e.g. "valid through [date]". I left it out because I don't know your terms.
3. **Segment if you can.** Send a version that leads with credit union sync to users who have a credit union (or who tried to connect one and failed). Everyone else gets the weekly summary first.
4. **Suppress.** Exclude anyone who has already reactivated or who is currently in a billing dispute. Check that the code is single-use per account and limited to lapsed users.

## Follow-up sequence

- **Day 4, if they didn't open:** Resend with the alternate subject line. Keep the body the same.
- **Day 8, if they opened but didn't click:** Send a 3-line email: "Here's what your first weekly summary would look like" with a screenshot, plus the code and the expiry.
- **Day 12 (final):** "Code expires [date]." Send it only to people who haven't converted, and make it very short.
- **After that:** Sunset anyone who didn't engage with any of the three. Continued sends hurt your deliverability.

I can also write the follow-ups in full, a plain-text-only version, or a version for credit-union-specific users.
